verdict.rationale: Crossplane exposes declarative, auditable APIs enforced via Kubernetes RBAC, and its marketing explicitly claims these APIs can be safely acted on by 'automation and AI systems,' which supports least-privilege access control at the API layer. However, there is no documented review-gate or approval workflow specific to AI agents (e.g., a plan/apply staging step, diff approval, or agent-scoped credential issuance) — the RBAC and declarative-API claims are generic platform-engineering primitives, not an agent-oriented guardrail feature. missing for 10: concrete agent-specific review/approval gate mechanism, documented least-privilege credential issuance workflow for agents, independent evidence of this being used to block unapproved AI-driven changes.
